title: A trip past the planets.
lines: Lotte is in bed, but she can't sleep.
Through the window she looks at the stars.
Daddy, she asks, what's out there in space?
Daddy sits down on the edge of the bed.
We get into a rocket, says Daddy.
A big, white rocket, with a red tip.
Ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one.
The rocket shoots up into the sky.
Lotte can feel it in her tummy.
The sky gets darker and darker.
It's completely black, with twinkling stars everywhere.
You drift around, just like in water.
There's a big blue ball, with white clouds and green patches.
There's our house, and school, and Grandma.
Then we fly to the moon first.
The moon is grey and full of craters.
There's no air and no water.
You can jump really high there.
Now we come to the planets.
All the planets go around the sun, like children in a big circle around the teacher.
There's red dust and there are high mountains.
There are little robots on Mars that people have sent.
They drive around and take photos.
Then we come to the very biggest planet.
Jupiter is so big that the Earth would fit inside it a thousand times.
It has stripes, orange and white and brown.
And it has a big red spot.
That's a storm that has been blowing for a very long time.
And then, says Daddy, the most beautiful planet of all.
Saturn has rings all around it.
Big, sparkling rings, made of ice and little rocks.
It looks like a hat with a wide brim.
Can I slide on the ring?
In our heads anything is possible!
After that it gets colder and colder.
Because we're very far from the sun.
You'd want your thick coat there.
Brrr, says Lotte, and she pulls her blanket up higher.
The sun is actually a star too, says Daddy.
A really big one, and very close.
That's why it's so bright and so warm.
All the other stars are suns too.
But they're so far away that they look very small.
More than all the grains of sand on the beach.
Then it's time to go back.
We fly past Saturn, past Jupiter, past Mars.
And there's the big blue ball.
When I grow up I'll be an astronaut.
Lotte looks at the stars one last time.
